def:virtual-subword:
Definition Virtual subword, entanglement across a cut, and connected parts. Let G be a group, standing for the braid group B_n or its image in the Hecke algebra H_n(q), and let R be a ring of values. A function f \colon G \to R is an observable if f(xy) = f(yx) for all x, y \in G. Words a, b are conjugate, a \approx b, if b = y a y^{-1} for some y, and equal in normal form, a \equiv b, if they reduce to the same Gröbner–Shirshov normal form.

Fix a set \mathcal{O} of observables. A subword x placed between u and v is virtual for \mathcal{O} if

  f(u\,x\,v) = f(u\,v) \quad \text{for every } f \in \mathcal{O}.

Let w be a word on n strands and A \subset \{1, \dots, n\}. Write c_A(w) for the signed number of crossings between a strand in A and a strand outside A, and s_A(w) for the signed number of the remaining crossings. The word is entangled across A \mid A^{c} if c_A(w) \neq 0. A prior entangled pair is a pure subword that is entangled across the cut separating its two partners.

Let F assign a value in a commutative ring to each finite set T of strands. Its connected part on T is the Möbius inversion over subsets,

  \phi_F(T) = (-1)^{|T|} \sum_{U \subseteq T} (-1)^{|U|} F(U).
rem:virtual-subword-remark:
Remark Virtual subwords, cut entanglement and the Borromean connected part. Observables. Equivalently, f is a class function: f(ywy^{-1}) = f(w). Every Markov trace and every irreducible character \chi_\lambda of H_n(q) is an observable in this sense.

Equality in normal form implies conjugacy, and the converse fails. Observables see only \approx.

Two kinds are virtual for every set of observables:

  1. Pair creation: x = y\,y^{-1}.
  2. Emission and reabsorption: a loop y\,w\,y^{-1} around a word w satisfies f(y\,w\,y^{-1}) = f(w) for every observable f.

A virtual subword is part of the word but changes no observable. Nothing in this definition calls it a particle, so it carries no propagator.

Entanglement across a cut. Every crossing of w is counted in exactly one of c_A(w) and s_A(w), so

  \mathrm{wr}(w) = c_A(w) + s_A(w).

For a pure braid, c_A(w) is twice the linking number between the two groups of strands.

Trivial-block shift. In the one-dimensional trivial block of H_n(q), where \sigma_i \mapsto q and \sigma_i^{-1} \mapsto q^{-1}, every word evaluates to

  q^{\mathrm{wr}(w)} = q^{c_A(w)} \cdot q^{s_A(w)}.

The shift therefore splits into an entangled part and a self-twist part. A shift q^{\pm 2} comes from either an entangled pair or a self-twist, and the block alone cannot tell which.

Pairwise entanglement is not enough. On three strands take V = \sigma_0 \sigma_1^{-1}. The word V^3 is pure, and every one-versus-two cut has c_A(V^3) = 0. Yet V^3 \neq 1, since its image under the reduced Burau representation at t = 2 is not the identity. Its closure is the Borromean rings. The entanglement of V^3 is three-party: it is detected by the Milnor invariant \bar\mu_{123} and not by any pairwise linking number. A complete definition of entanglement therefore needs the Milnor hierarchy. Pairwise linking is its first level, which corresponds to a Bell-type pair, while \bar\mu_{123} corresponds to a GHZ-type triple.

Connected part. On a pair this is \phi_F(\{a,b\}) = F(\{a,b\}) - F(\{a\}) - F(\{b\}) + F(\varnothing). Suppose T splits into disjoint nonempty parts T_1 and T_2 with F(U) = F(U \cap T_1) + F(U \cap T_2) for every U \subseteq T. Then \phi_F(T) = 0. So \phi_F(T) \neq 0 means that the strands of T do not split into two non-interacting groups, and it certifies |T|-party entanglement relative to F. Both statements are proved in the formalisation without extra hypotheses.

The natural choice of F comes from a knot invariant that turns split union into a product. For the Jones polynomial, G(L) = \delta\, V_L(t) with \delta = -(t^{1/2} + t^{-1/2}) satisfies G(L_1 \sqcup L_2) = G(L_1)\, G(L_2) and G(\text{unknot}) = \delta. Take F(T) = \log G(L_T) - |T| \log \delta for nonempty T, where L_T is the closure of the sub-braid on the strands of T, and set F(\varnothing) = 0. Then F vanishes on every unlink and is additive on split sublinks. The case |T| = 2 is the pairwise (Bell) level, and the case |T| = 3 with every pair contribution zero is the three-party (GHZ) level. The connected part has the same Möbius form as the connected three-body term of the binding sum. Whether the two are the same object is not established here.

For V^3 every sublink with at most two components is an unlink, so all single and pair contributions vanish and

  \phi_F(\{1,2,3\}) = \log \frac{V_{\mathrm{Bor}}(t)}{\delta^2}
  = \log\!\left(1 - \frac{(t-1)^4 (t^2+t+1)}{t^2 (t+1)^2}\right)
  = -\tfrac{3}{4} (\log t)^4 + O\big((\log t)^6\big).

This is exact over \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1/2}]. It vanishes at t = 1, so the classical limit cannot see the three-party entanglement, and it is nonzero for every t > 0 with t \neq 1.

sec:cp-violation-evidence:
Definition of CP violation. CP symmetry enforces perfect mirroring between matter and antimatter. CP violation fundamentally distinguishes them.

Experimental evidence.

Three systems establish CP violation:

  1. Neutral kaons (1964). Cronin and Fitch observed K_L \to \pi^+\pi^- at a rate of \sim 2 \times 10^{-3} [christenson1964].
  2. B mesons (2001). BaBar [aubert2001] and Belle measured CP-violating asymmetries in B^0 \to J/\psi\, K_S, confirming the complex CKM phase \delta_{\mathrm{CKM}}.
  3. D mesons (2019). LHCb measured CP violation in charm decays.

The matter-antimatter asymmetry.

Sakharov required C and CP violation for baryogenesis. The Standard Model CKM phase is quantitatively insufficient to explain the n_B / n_\gamma \sim 6 \times 10^{-10} ratio.

QOU interpretation.

In the complex chirality rotation framework the aether parameter is complex, q = |q|e^{i\theta}, and the matter-antimatter asymmetry is measured by the discriminant of the two crossing-energy magnitudes,

\delta_{\mathrm{CP}} = \frac{\lVert\mathfrak{E}_+\rVert - \lVert\mathfrak{E}_-\rVert}{\lVert\mathfrak{E}_+\rVert + \lVert\mathfrak{E}_-\rVert}.

The phase does not enter it. Writing the particle's crossing energy as n q and the mirror's as -n/q, per crossing energy on an all-positive braid together with antiparticle crossing reversal, the discriminant of their norms is

\delta_{\mathrm{CP}} = \frac{r^2 - 1}{r^2 + 1}, \qquad r = \lvert q\rvert,

for every \theta. This is an exact identity, not a leading order: \theta is bound on the left-hand side and absent from the right. At the aether anchor \delta_{\mathrm{CP}} \approx 0.10396, which coincides with \tanh(\ln r) and with the count-to-signed channel ratio of the n_- = 0 crossing sector.

The asymmetry is therefore supplied by r > 1 — the aether being deformed at all — and not by a residual phase. Consequently:

  • The observable sector projects \theta \to 0, and an imperfect projection leaves \theta_{\mathrm{res}}; but the discriminant is blind to it.
  • The \mathcal{O}(\theta_{\mathrm{res}}^2) scaling for single-crossing systems (e^-e^+) is refuted — the quantity is independent of \theta at every order, not only at leading order.
  • A geometric origin for the CKM phase does not follow from this discriminant, which carries no phase information.
  • The multi-crossing accumulation \delta_{\mathrm{CP}} \sim n_c\theta_{\mathrm{res}} is a statement about composites and is not addressed by the single-crossing-pair identity above. It is neither established nor refuted here.

Quantitative gap.

The crossing energy decomposition provides an EM-to-strong ratio of \tanh(\ln r) \approx 0.104. Since the discriminant carries no residual phase, the framework's value is \delta_{\mathrm{CP}} \approx 0.10396 itself, not \tanh(\ln r)\cdot\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} \approx 7.5866 \times 10^{-4}. Against the kaon \varepsilon \approx 2\times10^{-3} the ratio is \approx 52: the framework does not reproduce the kaon value.

Against the observed baryon-to-photon ratio \eta \approx 6.1\times10^{-10} the framework's asymmetry is too large, by a factor \approx 1.7\times10^{8}. The open object is therefore a suppression f = \eta/\delta_{\mathrm{CP}} \approx 5.87\times10^{-9} — an entropy or washout factor — and not a further asymmetry. That search direction is constrained: the bar-odd part of \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}] is free of rank one over its bar-even part, generated by q - q^{-1}, so no second bar-odd shape is available. A ratio of counts is a different kind of quantity from an amplitude.

prop:algebraic-gns-embedding:
Proposition Markov-trace GNS embedding H_\infty(q)/\mathcal{N} \hookrightarrow L(\mathcal{H}) — operator-algebra route to the Archimedean side. Let q > 0 be real, and give H_\infty(q) the *-structure fixed by \sigma_i^* = \sigma_i (extended conjugate-linearly and anti-multiplicatively). The QOU aether q_0 \approx 1.11 is such a q. The infinite Hecke algebra H_\infty(q) := \varinjlim_n H_n(R, q) carries a unique tracial state \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_\infty(q) \to R\otimes\mathbb{R} satisfying positivity \mathrm{tr}_M(x^* x) \geq 0. Write \mathcal{N} := \{x \in H_\infty(q) : \mathrm{tr}_M(x^* x) = 0\} for its trace ideal. The GNS construction yields a separable Hilbert space \mathcal{H} and a faithful *-representation of the trace-quotient

  \pi_{\mathrm{GNS}} \colon H_\infty(q)/\mathcal{N} \;\hookrightarrow\;
    L(\mathcal{H}).

This realises the pre-Archimedean aether as a concrete operator algebra.

Note (the quotient is non-trivial). At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the trace ideal is non-zero: \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda with y_\lambda = 0 precisely when \ell(\lambda) \geq 3, so \mathcal{N} is the Temperley–Lieb radical and H_\infty(q)/\mathcal{N} \cong \mathrm{TL}_\infty(q). Faithfulness therefore holds on the quotient rather than on H_\infty(q) itself.

Positivity domain. Because [2]_q = q + q^{-1} \geq 2 for every real q > 0, trace positivity on the Temperley–Lieb quotient holds unconditionally for all q > 0.
prf:algebraic-gns-embedding:
Proof Proof of the Markov-trace GNS embedding. Four standard components are assembled.

Tower of inclusions. The Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) has presentation by braid generators \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1} modulo the braid relations and the quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1. The inclusion H_n(q) \hookrightarrow H_{n+1}(q) adjoins \sigma_n. This inclusion is unital, R-linear, and commutes with the *-structure \sigma_i^* = \sigma_i. (This is the *-structure for which positivity below holds; it is distinct from the bar involution \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}, q \mapsto q^{-1}, which does not fix z = q^3/(q^2+1).) The sequence \{H_n(q)\}_{n \geq 1} forms a filtered inductive system of unital *-algebras over R, with colimit H_\infty(q) = \bigcup_n H_n(q) [jones1985].

Markov property. The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_{M,n} \colon H_n(q) \to R satisfies the recursion \mathrm{tr}_{M,n+1}(x \cdot \sigma_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M,n}(x) for any x \in H_n(q), where z = q^3/(q^2+1) (Jones–Markov trace). Equivalently, \mathrm{tr}_{M,n+1}|_{H_n(q)} = \mathrm{tr}_{M,n}. This compatibility with the inclusions defines a unique R\otimes\mathbb{Q}-linear trace \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_\infty(q) \to R\otimes\mathbb{Q} extending all \mathrm{tr}_{M,n} by the universal property of the colimit.

Positivity. Let q > 0 be real. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the Markov trace vanishes on every Wedderburn block with three or more rows, so it factors through the Temperley–Lieb quotient \mathrm{TL}_n(\delta) with loop value \delta = [2]_q = q + q^{-1}. Jones proved that the Markov trace on \mathrm{TL}_n(\delta) is a positive functional, \mathrm{tr}_{M,n}(x^* x) \geq 0, whenever \delta \geq 2 [jones1985]. Here q + q^{-1} \geq 2 for every real q > 0, with equality only at q = 1. So \mathrm{tr}_M is a positive trace on H_\infty(q) for every real q > 0, and in particular at q_0. There is no threshold in q to be near.

In Wedderburn terms, \mathrm{tr}_{M,n} = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda, and on each block the trace is y_\lambda times the matrix trace in Wenzl's orthogonal (seminormal) representation, where each \sigma_i acts by a real symmetric matrix [wenzl1988]. Positivity is then y_\lambda \geq 0 for every \lambda. The closed-form Ocneanu weight at z = q^3/(q^2+1) is strictly positive on every shape with at most two rows, for q > 0, q \neq 1, and zero on the rest. That this closed form is the Markov weight at general n is the classical Ocneanu–Wenzl formula; it is proved here only at n = 3 and checked numerically through n = 6, so the positivity statement supports the cited result and does not replace it.

GNS construction. Define the left ideal \mathcal{N} := \{x \in H_\infty(q) : \mathrm{tr}_M(x^* x) = 0\}. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) this ideal is not trivial: \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda with y_\lambda = 0 precisely when \ell(\lambda) \geq 3, so \mathcal{N} is the sum of those Wedderburn blocks — the Temperley–Lieb radical — and the GNS quotient is H_\infty(q)/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_\infty(q), not H_\infty(q) itself. Positivity and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality |\mathrm{tr}_M(x^* y)|^2 \leq \mathrm{tr}_M(x^* x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y^* y) guarantee \mathcal{N} is a well-defined ideal. The quotient V := H_\infty(q) / \mathcal{N} forms an H_\infty(q)-module under left multiplication. The bilinear form \langle [x], [y] \rangle := \mathrm{tr}_M(x^* y) is sesquilinear and positive definite on V. Its completion \mathcal{H} is a separable Hilbert space. Separability follows because H_\infty(q) admits a countable basis as an R\otimes\mathbb{Q}-module.

The left-multiplication action \pi_{\mathrm{GNS}}(a)[x] := [a x] extends to a bounded operator on \mathcal{H}. The trace Cauchy–Schwarz inequality yields the bound \|\pi_{\mathrm{GNS}}(a)\| \leq \|a\|_2. The representation is faithful: \pi_{\mathrm{GNS}}(a) = 0 implies \pi_{\mathrm{GNS}}(a)[1] = [a] = 0, requiring a \in \mathcal{N}, which means \mathrm{tr}_M(a^* a) = 0, and thus a = 0 in the trace-quotient. The *-property \pi_{\mathrm{GNS}}(a^*) = \pi_{\mathrm{GNS}}(a)^* holds on the dense subspace V \subset \mathcal{H} and extends to \mathcal{H} by continuity. \square

prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton:
Proposition Asymptotic skeleton of the q-Plancherel measure \mathbb{M}_{n,q} — convergence on a continuous Young-diagram space. Let \mathbb{M}_{n,q} denote the q-Plancherel measure on partitions of n,

  \mathbb{M}_{n,q}(\lambda)
  \;=\; \frac{q^{n(\lambda)}\, f^\lambda}
             {\prod_{\square \in \lambda} \{h(\square)\}_q},
  \qquad
  \{k\}_q \;=\; \frac{q^k - 1}{q - 1},
  \quad
  n(\lambda) \;=\; \sum_i (i-1)\lambda_i ,

with f^\lambda the number of standard Young tableaux and h(\square) the hook lengths. Here n(\lambda) is Macdonald's partition statistic, not a function of the size n — the two are distinct objects sharing a glyph, and the size is always the bare n. Write \lambda' for the conjugate (transposed) partition and c(\square) = j - i for the content of the box in row i, column j. The blackboard-bold \mathbb{M} follows the \mathbb{V} precedent in the notation register: it is the source literature's own symbol, raised out of plain M and \mathcal{M}, both of which are claimed here (the latter by the mass endomorphism). Define a topological space \mathcal{K}_q (the q-deformed Kerov limit-shape space) and pushforward maps

  \iota_n \colon \{\lambda \vdash n\}
    \;\longrightarrow\; \mathcal{K}_q,
  \qquad
  n \in \mathbb{N},

such that \mu_n^{(q)} := (\iota_n)_*\,\mathbb{M}_{n,q} satisfy:

  1. (Existence at q = 1.) The sequence \{\mu_n^{(1)}\} converges weakly to \mu_\infty^{(1)} [vershik-kerov1977, biane1998].
  2. (Asymptotics at generic q.) The row lengths obey a law of large numbers, \lambda_i/n \to (1-q)q^{i-1} in probability, and their fluctuations are asymptotically Gaussian at scale \sqrt{n} [feray-meliot2012].
  3. (Limit identification, conjectural.) For q \neq 1, \{\mu_n^{(q)}\} converges weakly to \mu_\infty^{(q)}. Identify \mu_\infty^{(q)} with a measure on \pi_{\mathrm{GNS}}(H_\infty(q)).

Which weight this is, and why it changed

Identification of \mathbb{M}_{n,q} with the Molien fake-degree measure. Note that the Plancherel measure \mathbb{M}_{n,q} governing clause 2 is distinct from the squared-quantum-dimension weight w_\lambda^{(n)}(q) = \dim_q^2(\lambda)/[n]_q!; rather, \mathbb{M}_{n,q} coincides with the Molien fake-degree weight, which satisfies

  \frac{f^\lambda \, q^{-\kappa_\lambda} \, \dim_q(\lambda)}{[n]_q!}
  \;=\; \mathbb{M}_{n,\,q^2}(\lambda),
  \qquad
  \kappa_\lambda \;=\; \sum_{\square \in \lambda} c(\square),

verified in exact rational arithmetic for every partition of n = 1,\dots,9. So this proposition is not being restated over a new object; it is being restated over one the corpus has had all along, with the substitution Q = q^2 making the identification.

The exponent \kappa_\lambda is forced, not chosen. Substituting Q = q^2 into the display above leaves q^{2n(\lambda) - \sum_\square h(\square) + n}, which collapses to q^{-\kappa_\lambda} by two identities — \sum_\square h(\square) = n(\lambda) + n(\lambda') + n and \kappa_\lambda = n(\lambda') - n(\lambda) — each verified independently over all partitions of n \leq 10 in the same probe. Without them the identity would be an agreement at 96 sample points; with them it is a derivation.

This also explains a coincidence the corpus carried without comment: the proved identity \sum_\lambda f^\lambda q^{-\kappa_\lambda}\dim_q(\lambda) = [n]_q! holds for every n, and \mathbb{M}_{n,q} is a probability measure by construction. Those are the same theorem.

The aether sits at q > 1, and that costs an orientation, not the theorem

[feray-meliot2012] states its asymptotics for q < 1, while the aether gives Q = q_0^2 \approx 1.2321. The paper's own duality \mathbb{M}_{n,q^{-1}}(\lambda') = \mathbb{M}_{n,q}(\lambda) closes the gap: it is an exact identity, verified here over all partitions of n \leq 9 in exact arithmetic, so the Q > 1 results are the Q^{-1} < 1 results read on conjugate diagrams. Clause 2 at the aether therefore describes the columns of \lambda where the cited statement describes rows. Nothing is lost and nothing is approximated; only a transposition is needed.

Deformed precedents for clause 3, and what each would need (literature)

Two published routes reach a limit-shape and fluctuation theorem for a deformed Plancherel measure. Neither covers \mathbb{M}_{n,q}, and neither has had its hypotheses checked for it.

The Jack deformation. Replacing symmetric-group characters by Jack characters with parameter \alpha > 0 (\alpha = 1 recovers the classical case) gives a deformed Plancherel measure whose bulk has a deterministic limit shape and Gaussian fluctuations [dolega-feray2014, §1.1--§1.2], and the construction extends to a general measure P^\chi attached to a family of characters on partitions [dolega-sniady2018, §1.4--§1.7]. The tool that makes the argument run is that the structure constants of Jack characters are polynomial in the deformation parameter [dolega-feray2014, §1.5, §4]. The Jack parameter is a different deformation from q, so this is a template, not a proof: a q-analogue along this route would first need a polynomiality or degree bound on the structure constants of the characters that define \mathbb{M}_{n,q}.

Approximate factorization. Biane proves concentration for any normalized positive-definite function \psi on the symmetric group whose values on a permutation \rho of support size l are bounded by c_l N^{-l/2} and approximately factorize on disjointly supported permutations: the induced measure on Young diagrams concentrates, and character values satisfy |\chi^\lambda(\rho) - \psi(\rho)| \le K(\delta + N^{-1})^{1/4} N^{-l/2} [biane2000, Def. 1.3, Thms 1--2]. Here N is the size of the symmetric group, written q in the source; it is unrelated to the deformation parameter q of this block. Using this route would require exhibiting \mathbb{M}_{n,q} as the measure of such a \psi and checking both bounds, which has not been done.

What is still open

The transfer to w_\lambda^{(n)}(q) = \dim_q^2/[n]_q! is unestablished, and that family is still in production. Restating this block does not migrate plancherel-term-7-formulation, whose \Phi_k functional is defined against a \dim_q^2 family. The canonical numerator for \Phi_k is the Molien weight f^\lambda q^{-\kappa_\lambda}\dim_q(\lambda)/[n]_q!, with the self-normalised \dim_q^2/\sum_\mu \dim_q^2 kept as a labelled comparison arm; what remains is to migrate the functional onto it. The choice is not cosmetic: the same harness ranks three different distinguished knots at k = 3 under three of the candidate families.

Clause 3 remains conjectural, isolating two open problems: q-deformed Kerov–Vershik convergence, and the operator-algebra realisation of the limit.

prf:centered-hecke-variance-positive:
Proof Proof: centred Hecke variance is strictly positive. Apply the Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 and the Markov property:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i^2)
  = (q - q^{-1}) \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) + 1
  = (q - q^{-1}) z + 1.

Hence

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\tilde\sigma_i^2)
  =
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i^2 - 2 z \sigma_i + z^2)
  =
  (q - q^{-1}) z + 1 - 2 z^2 + z^2
  =
  (q - q^{-1}) z + 1 - z^2.

This is the variance. Both steps are convention-independent: they use only the quadratic relation and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = z.

Closed form. Substituting z = q^3/(q^2+1) and q - q^{-1} = (q^2-1)/q:

  (q - q^{-1})\,z \;=\; \frac{q^2(q^2-1)}{q^2+1},
  \qquad
  z^2 \;=\; \frac{q^6}{(q^2+1)^2}.

Over the common denominator (q^2+1)^2,

  \mathrm{Var}(\sigma_i)
  \;=\; \frac{q^2(q^2-1)(q^2+1) + (q^2+1)^2 - q^6}{(q^2+1)^2}
  \;=\; \frac{q^6 - q^2 + q^4 + 2q^2 + 1 - q^6}{(q^2+1)^2}
  \;=\; \frac{q^4 + q^2 + 1}{(q^2+1)^2}.

Positivity. Numerator and denominator are both strictly positive for every real q, so \mathrm{Var}(\sigma_i) > 0 unconditionally — no regime hypothesis is needed. For the sharp bound, set t = q^2 > 0 and write f(t) = (t^2+t+1)/(t+1)^2. Then

  f'(t) \;=\; \frac{t-1}{(t+1)^3},

which is negative on (0,1), zero at t = 1, and positive on (1,\infty). So f attains its global minimum at t = 1, i.e. q = 1, where f(1) = 3/4, and f(t) \to 1 as t \to 0^+ and as t \to \infty. Therefore

  \tfrac{3}{4} \;\leq\; \mathrm{Var}(\sigma_i) \;<\; 1
  \qquad \text{for all } q > 0,

with equality on the left only at q = 1. At q_0 the value is 0.75270211325196540159. \square

Identification. The closed form is not a new quantity. Since [2]_q = (q^2+1)/q and [4]_q = [2]_q(q^2+q^{-2}),

  \frac{[4]_q}{[2]_q^3} + \frac{1}{[2]_q^2}
  \;=\; \frac{q^4+1}{(q^2+1)^2} + \frac{q^2}{(q^2+1)^2}
  \;=\; \frac{q^4+q^2+1}{(q^2+1)^2},

so \mathrm{Var}(\sigma_i) = y_{(3)} + y_{(2,1)} = \mu_+ identically in q — the centred second moment of a single Hecke generator is the isospin-triplet Wenzl weight.

prf:brane-tower-q-laplacian-decay:
Proof Proof of the brane-tower convergence bound. The absolute-convergence bound follows by direct geometric-series estimation on the iterated Laplacian.

Step 1: q-integer asymptotic. For q > 1, the q-integer [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) satisfies

  [k]_q \;=\; \frac{q^k}{q - q^{-1}}\,\bigl(1 - q^{-2k}\bigr)
  \;\leq\;
  \frac{q^k}{q - q^{-1}}.

Squaring and applying \hbar_q = (q - 1)/q gives \lambda_k^{(q)} = [k]_q^2 \hbar_q / L_q^2 \leq C\,q^{2k} for a constant C = \hbar_q / \bigl((q - q^{-1})^2 L_q^2\bigr).

Step 2: Single-jet bound. The \hbar_q^2 \Delta^{(1)} term on a normalised mode e_k of the Reeb bundle yields

  \bigl|\langle e_k, \hbar_q^2 \Delta^{(1)} e_k \rangle\bigr|
  \;=\;
  \hbar_q^2 \, \lambda_k^{(q)}
  \;\leq\;
  \hbar_q^2 \cdot C \, q^{2k}.

For the leading mode k = 1, this quantity is finite. Higher modes produce exponentially suppressed corrections, controlled in Step 4.

Step 3: Iterated-Laplacian bound. The n-th iteration \Delta^{(n)} on the same mode yields

  \bigl|\langle e_k, \Delta^{(n)} e_k\rangle\bigr|
  \;=\;
  (\lambda_k^{(q)})^n
  \;\leq\;
  C^n \, q^{2nk}.

Thus, the \hbar_q^{2n} tower coefficient on mode k is at most

  \hbar_q^{2n} \cdot C^n \, q^{2nk}
  \;=\;
  \bigl(\hbar_q^2 \, C \, q^{2k}\bigr)^n.

Step 4: Geometric-series sum. Sum over n with k = 1 fixed to extract the dominant mode contribution. Use \hbar_q^2 C q^2 < 1, which holds for q \in (1, q_*) with q_* \approx 1.2. This range comfortably covers the aether q_0 \approx 1.110:

  \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \hbar_q^{2n} C^n q^{2n}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\hbar_q^2 \, C \, q^2}{1 - \hbar_q^2 \, C \, q^2}
  \;<\;\infty.

Step 5: Leading versus remainder. Separate the n = 1 term:

  T(\rho) - \hbar_q^2 \,\Delta^{(1)}(\rho)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \hbar_q^{2n} \, \Delta^{(n)}(\rho).

On the leading mode Step 3 is an equality, \langle e_1, \Delta^{(n)} e_1\rangle = \lambda_1^n with \lambda_1 = \lambda_1^{(q)} = \hbar_q / L_q^2. The uniform bound on \Delta^{(n)} makes \lambda_1^n bounded in n, and a bounded sequence of powers has \lambda_1 \leq 1. Therefore

  \bigl| T(\rho) - \hbar_q^2 \,\Delta^{(1)}(\rho) \bigr|
  \;\leq\;
  \|\rho\|_{L^2}
  \cdot
  \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \hbar_q^{2n} \lambda_1^{n}
  \;\leq\;
  \|\rho\|_{L^2}
  \cdot
  \frac{\hbar_q^4}{1 - \hbar_q^2}.

Finally \frac{1}{1 - \hbar_q^2} \leq \frac{q^{-2}}{1 - q^{-2}} on 1 < q \leq q_*. With x = q^{-1} and \hbar_q = 1 - x, this reads 1 - x^2 \leq 2x^3 - x^4. The difference f(x) = 2x^3 - x^4 + x^2 - 1 has f'(x) = 2x(1 + 3x - 2x^2) > 0 on (0, 1] and f(1/1.2) > 0, so it holds on [1/1.2, 1]. This yields the displayed bound.

Direct eigenvalue bound. Bounding the tail directly through the exact leading eigenvalue avoids absorbing the Step-1 constant C into C q^2 \leq q^{-2} (which would require L_q \geq q^2 \sqrt{\hbar_q}/(q - q^{-1}) \approx 1.855 rather than the normalized value L_q = \sqrt{\hbar_q}), and therefore requires no auxiliary condition on L_q beyond the uniform bound.

Sharpness. At q_0 \approx 1.110, \hbar_q \approx 0.099 and q^{-2} \approx 0.812. Therefore, the geometric ratio q^{-2} \hbar_q^2 \approx 0.008 \ll 1. The single-jet term dominates the tower at the \approx 1\% level. Three jet levels suffice for sub-ppm precision, justifying the truncations applied elsewhere in the mass-formula derivations. \square
